scope: Reconcile the current public DXF, ezdxf, OCCT, and FreeCAD routes into a fail-fast optional ACIS/B-rep qualification gate that distinguishes container handling, payload parsing, kernel semantics, and native application acceptance.

method.kind: Primary Autodesk format references and current upstream project documentation/source review
method.evidenceBoundary: Autodesk pages establish outer DXF fields only. Project docs establish their own declared route and limits, not successful parsing of this repository's payloads or B-rep validity. Mutable upstream pages are discovery evidence. No independent second-kernel, source-native known-size ACIS witness was produced by this review.

observed: 3DSOLID and REGION document AcDbModelerGeometry, group 70, and proprietary group-1/group-3 payload fields.
3DSOLID additionally has an entity-specific AcDb3dSolid subclass and group-350 history-object reference.
The published entity tables do not establish inner SAT/SAB save-version semantics or geometric validity.
evidence.planUse: Keep raw carrier order/hash, history association, semantic body construction, and consumer acceptance as distinct evidence stages.

observed: The current API documents SAT for DXF R2000-R2010 and SAB for R2013 and later, and permits SAT/SAB assignment to ACIS entities from R2000 onward.
Its documented ACIS entity target is a bounded flat-polyhedron subset; vertex-derived bounds are exact only for straight-edged polyhedra, and mesh projection loses curved faces.
evidence.planUse: Treat a pinned ezdxf run as structural, carrier, or bounded polyhedron evidence only; explicitly record the subset and do not infer general curved B-rep support.

evidence.topic: OCCT open core versus ACIS exchange component
observed: OCCT identifies its core as an open-source 3D modeling platform.
The separate OCCT Components repository calls itself a preview of commercial extensions and lists ACIS SAT/SAB import-export as an exchange component.
evidence.planUse: Do not assume FreeCAD/OCCT includes an ACIS reader. At the composed optional gate, first verify the exact component, version, platform, license/authorization, and callable structured-shape route. If unavailable or unauthorized, record NOT_AVAILABLE/NOT_RUN and continue without installation, purchase, trial, or dependency changes.

observed: FreeCAD documents a native C++ DXF importer and a separate legacy Python route, and describes DWG conversion as an external-converter path.
Current importDWG.py converts the DWG to DXF and then invokes importDXF.open/insert; its converter routes include LibreDWG, ODA File Converter, and QCAD.
These workflow facts do not establish ACIS/B-rep consumption or a release-wide entity contract.
evidence.planUse: Keep FreeCAD acceptance keyed by exact release, OS, converter, emitted DXF, importer backend, and final document geometry. Stock FreeCAD remains separate from a licensed modeler route.

nextActions: Continue existing local S2/S3/S5 implementation slices and fast tests without waiting on external route availability.
At the composed checkpoint, perform the metadata/license/platform and output-capability preflight before launching any optional external tool.
For eligible routes, record container parse, payload identity, topology, kernel validity/metrics, and native acceptance independently.
Do not count mesh, wireframe, bounding-box fallback, OCCT-derived same-kernel shape conversion, or an open-file result as independent ACIS B-rep qualification.

changes: Added a metadata-only fail-fast stop rule for optional semantic readers/kernels.
Separated route eligibility and licensing from implementation blockers and support evidence.
